status: RESOLVED -- previously blocked by an environment/tooling issue, now verified clean
clean_reverification_environment: Python 3.11.9, isolated worktree /tmp/fusion_fresh2 (created fresh post-reboot), fresh venv, fresh .mutmut-cache.
root_cause_of_original_block: Any coverage-instrumented pytest invocation with --cov targeting `compitum.applications.fusion.diiid_adapter` (or anything at/below the `compitum.applications.fusion` subpackage) crashed during test collection with `numpy: ImportError: cannot load module more than once per process`. This reproduced identically across 3 independent venvs, 2 Python versions (3.11 and 3.13), both pytest-cov and bare coverage.py, both the C-accelerated and pure-Python tracer, both Git-Bash and native PowerShell, and survived a full machine reboot -- ruling out venv corruption, resource exhaustion, and OS/process state. Root-caused by systematically swapping the --cov target: `--cov=compitum.applications` (the PARENT package, one level up from `fusion`) succeeds completely with 100% coverage on every file in the fusion subpackage, while any target at or below `fusion` itself crashes. This narrows the trigger to a specific interaction between coverage.py's own module-discovery/import mechanism for the --cov target and this package's structure -- likely related to `src/compitum/applications/__init__.py`'s shallow re-export (`from .fusion import PlasmaMonitor`), which causes `compitum.applications.fusion` to be imported via two different code paths (once implicitly through the parent's own re-export, once explicitly by coverage.py's target resolution) during measurement setup.
workaround: Use `--cov=compitum.applications` (the parent package) instead of the narrower `compitum.applications.fusion.diiid_adapter` target when running coverage-guided mutation testing for any file under `compitum/applications/fusion/`. This is a pure test-harness/orchestration workaround -- no production source was modified. Coverage data for the specific target file remains fully accurate (confirmed 100% line+branch coverage on diiid_adapter.py specifically, verified via the same command).
verdict: CLEAN -- zero survivors. This file's existing test suite (tests/applications/test_diiid_adapter_options.py and related) is fully adequate; the only issue was ever the coverage-target workaround needed to run mutation testing at all on this machine.
